messages.text:
What happen if unit becomes defective after 2 years. Can it be repair at my
local computer hardware store?

Hello,

Short answer: after the warranty window (our RMA cover is 3 months from delivery), a unit is yours to repair, and nothing we do stops you from having someone local look at it. Whether a computer shop can actually help depends entirely on which part failed.

The good news is that most failures on these miners after a year or two are not the mining silicon at all. They are the boring parts: the power supply, a fan with worn bearings, the DC barrel jack or power connector, the little display, or a USB or Ethernet port. All of that is standard electronics work, and a competent local repair shop with a soldering iron can handle it, or in the case of a PSU or fan you can simply buy a replacement with the same voltage, amperage and connector and swap it yourself. For a PSU the rule is match the voltage exactly and meet or exceed the amperage.

Where a general computer store will usually hit a wall is the hashboard itself: a dead ASIC chip, a cooked voltage regulator or TPS, or a short on the board. Those need BM13xx-family parts, hot air rework and a board-level diagnosis, so you want an ASIC repair specialist rather than a PC shop. Also worth knowing before you spend money: a unit that will not boot, hashes at a fraction of its rating, or drops offline is very often firmware, pool settings or network rather than hardware, and that costs nothing to rule out. Reflashing the latest firmware and doing a factory reset fixes a surprising share of what looks like a dead unit.

One caution: opening the case or running overclocked settings voids the warranty, so if you are still inside the cover window, let us look at it first rather than a third party.

If you ever get to that point, our Discord is the fastest place for repair advice, including people who have fixed the exact board you have. It is https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and you can mention @nullhashrate, who is our hardware lead. Tell me the model and what it is doing and I will go through it with you.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
